name: Kap Paper Kapuskasing MDF Facility Conversion
description: Kap Paper Inc. in Kapuskasing, Ontario is pursuing conversion of its mill to a medium-density fibreboard (MDF) facility. The Government of Canada is investing $7.5 million (January 2026) through the Strategic Response Fund for a Front End Engineering Design study, bringing combined federal support to $17.5 million including $10 million announced October 2025. Plant conversion forecast at up to 30 months.

name: Semiahmoo First Nation Community Infrastructure and Housing Development
description: A $6 million federal investment announced January 15, 2026 funds core infrastructure on Semiahmoo Indian Reserve No. 1 in the South Surrey-White Rock area — site servicing, water and wastewater services including a Beach Road watermain and fire hydrants, road access, and electrical upgrades — to enable a planned 32-unit housing development backed by $24.9 million from BC Housing. Infrastructure work was scheduled to begin March 2026, housing construction in 2027, and completion in 2028.

name: Jack Garland Airport PFAS Remediation
proponent: Department of National Defence / City of North Bay
description: DND announced in December 2025 an amended contribution agreement raising total funding to approximately $120 million for PFAS remediation at Jack Garland Airport in North Bay, contamination originating from firefighting foam used from the 1970s to mid-1990s. A first phase moved 26,000 tonnes of contaminated soil; the amended 16-year agreement funds about 97% of planned airport remediation work, plus a separate $8.25 million agreement for drinking water treatment plant PFAS pilot upgrades.

name: IMT Precision 155mm Artillery Shell Manufacturing Facility
description: On March 18, 2026, the federal government announced up to $306.4 million under the Canadian Defence Industry Resilience Program for IMT Precision to build a new manufacturing plant producing metal shells for 155-millimetre artillery projectiles, expected to create at least 300 full-time positions. Site selection for the new facility was under review at announcement; IMT's existing operations are in Ingersoll, Ontario.

name: Saint-Hyacinthe Wastewater Treatment Plant Modernization
description: The governments of Canada and Quebec increased their combined funding for the upgrade of Saint-Hyacinthe's 1980s-era wastewater treatment plant to $49.85 million ($24.9 million each), announced November 25, 2025. The modernization includes primary settling tank mechanical upgrades, main building roof repairs, and automation system modernization; the city targets a treatment capacity increase of at least 50% with construction running approximately two years from winter 2025.

name: Mont-Tremblant Downtown Wastewater Treatment Plant Expansion and Modernization
description: Mont-Tremblant is investing $36.5 million, financed through a 30-year loan bylaw, to expand and modernize its downtown wastewater treatment plant, adding a second clarifier, renovating existing facilities, and adding redundancy equipment. The tender process is underway with contract award expected by end of spring 2026 and construction beginning summer 2026 over two years, to meet Quebec environmental standards taking effect by December 2030.
